reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to confirm CTLA-4 engagement by ipilimumab. However, ipilimumab is a well-established CTLA-4 antibody with known mechanism, so target engagement is likely but unconfirmed in this trial. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or immune activation markers reported to confirm downstream T-cell activation or immune response enhancement. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: This is a single-arm Phase 2 trial with 21 patients reporting 66.7% 1-year OS rate. Without a control arm or historical comparison provided, it's impossible to determine if this represents efficacy. The lack of p-value and comparator makes clinical benefit assessment impossible. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported in this small single-arm study. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Major issues include single-arm design preventing efficacy assessment, very small sample size (N=21), and high toxicity burden with 66.7% experiencing elevated ALT and 46.7% elevated AST (both serious adverse events), plus multiple immune-related AEs leading to treatment discontinuations.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm Phase 2 design with no control group, no historical comparison provided, no p-value reported, and no biomarker data to assess target engagement or pathway modulation. Cannot determine if 66.7% 1-year OS represents efficacy without comparator.
